public_rationale: Every year-to-year comparison I could document goes the way he said, and none goes against him. Anthropic's S-1 shows 2024 burn well above 2023 on every measure: operating cash used up $4.1 billion, operating loss $551 million to $2.98 billion, net loss $1.53 billion to $8.31 billion. OpenAI's loss doubled to $540 million in 2022 and was about $5 billion in 2024. But the claim says 'every single year'. I found no reliable 2023 figure for OpenAI and no figures for Anthropic's 2021 or 2022. So I cannot confirm each step. The evidence leans toward the claim, but it does not settle it.
limitations: The measures are mixed (net loss, operating loss, operating cash flow) because no single measure is available for every year.
The OpenAI figures come from news reports and leaked statements, not published filings.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic’s burn increased every single year! So has OpenAI's!

from_speaker: Anthropic’s burn increased every single year
our_interpretation: 'Burn' is read broadly, in line with the author's usage in the passage, which includes non-cash costs. Annual net loss, operating loss or operating cash outflow each count as a measure of burn. A year-on-year rise on the measure available for each pair of years counts as an increase.

'Every single year' covers each year-to-year change from the company's founding or first operating years up to 2024, the last full year before the post. For Anthropic that is 2021 to 2024. For OpenAI it is at least 2021 to 2024, the period of its commercial scale-up for which figures are reported.
The claim is graded supported only if every year-to-year change in that span can be shown to be an increase. One documented decrease contradicts it. Missing years leave it unresolved.
criteria.support_condition: For both companies, reported annual burn (losses or cash outflow) rose in every year-to-year change through 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: For either company, a reported annual burn figure fell from one year to the next before or in 2024.
